faq.answer: No. Intensity may arise from unresolved harm, unequal labor, attachment threat, power, stress, or poor conflict skills. The subtype hypothesis requires repeated One correction attention plus matched comparisons and reciprocal standards.
faq.question: Does intense criticism in a relationship prove one-to-one Type One?

faq.answer: Consent distinguishes collaborative change from pressure. Record whether the other person can decline, propose another standard, or end the discussion safely. A typology label never overrides boundaries, autonomy, or evidence of harm.
faq.question: Why is consent part of the observation?

faq.answer: Use the same issue across settings. Focused reform directs urgency toward a particular person or bond; social Type One directs attention toward rules and examples for a group. Role authority and relationship history may still explain either pattern.
faq.question: How can focused reform be compared with social Type One?

sections.body_md: The hypothesis combines Type One standards-and-correction attention with a one-to-one label for concentrated energy toward a particular bond or person. Intensity alone is ambiguous; attachment, conflict history, authority, attraction, caregiving, or immediate harm can focus the same behavior.
sections.title: Treat focused reform as provisional

sections.body_md: A matched comparison contrasts focused reform with self-preservation upkeep and social rule-setting. Keep the problem similar, then observe whether attention first targets one person's change, practical maintenance and reserves, or a standard that should govern the wider group.
sections.title: Match one issue across three priorities

sections.body_md: One-to-one is traditional vocabulary, not a biological drive, neurological capacity, fixed intensity trait, or compatibility measure. The label cannot establish relationship quality, attraction, consent, safety, or who should remain together.
sections.title: Reject biological certainty and compatibility claims

sections.body_md: Subtype traditions differ about intensity, anger, and countertypical presentations. Specify the observable proposition rather than importing a whole portrait, and let contradictory events or a clearer relational explanation change the working hypothesis.
sections.title: Name variation across traditions

sections.body_md: A damaged agreement, unequal responsibility, mentoring duty, repeated boundary breach, or safety concern can concentrate correction on one person. Compare other relationships and observe what changes after power, consent, and immediate risk are addressed.
sections.title: Test relationship history and power

sections.body_md: A one-to-one Type One counterexample weakens focused reform when urgency vanishes after status changes, standards apply only to the other person, or the person consistently prioritizes private upkeep and public rules over changing a particular bond.
sections.title: Use reciprocal flexibility as a challenge

sections.body_md: Instrument-specific evidence does not establish universal subtype ontology or cross-cultural equivalence. This draft cannot diagnose either person, predict compatibility or relationship outcomes, certify consent, complete human review, or authorize release.
sections.title: Keep relational inference modest

sections.body_md:
Duration: 4

Context: Choose one recurring disagreement with clear consent to reflect, plus two comparable issues involving a group rule and a practical maintenance task.

Observable signal: Record whose change receives urgency, whether the standard is reciprocal, how refusal is handled, and which concrete repair follows.

Page-specific signal: Compare focused reform of one bond with group-wide standard-setting and private upkeep while keeping the underlying issue as similar as possible.

Alternative explanation: Test conflict history, unequal labor, attraction, mentoring duty, power, boundary breaches, immediate risk, and communication skill against the subtype.

Reflection prompt: Identify the event where urgency followed power or history rather than reciprocal standards and state which explanation should replace or weaken the subtype.

seo.description: One-to-one Type One is a traditional type-by-instinct hypothesis in which One attention to correction may become especially concentrated in a particular relationship, commitment, or person's change. One focused reform is observable, but it is not proof of biological intensity, compatibility, or a universal subtype.
seo.title: One-to-one Type One: focused reform as a traditional hypothesis
